title: Study of the Influence of Sleep on Hemodynamic Parameters in Patients With Sleep Disorders
brief_summary: Several epidemiological studies in large cohorts suggest a strong association between sleep duration, complaint of insomnia and risk of hypertension.These findings suggest an important role of sleep quality in development of hypertension. Principal limitations of these studies are the cross-sectional study design, self-report sleep duration and poor measurement of blood pressure. The investigators propose to study an insomniac population with complete evaluation of quality and quantity of sleep, associated to complete hemodynamic measurement of hypertension.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* adult with insomnia (6 months or more)

Exclusion Criteria:

* sleep disorders with obstructive apnea
study_population: adult with chronic complain of insomnia
